page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5i-c2g1.large is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. This instance features 2 dedicated physical CPU cores with a single thread per core, providing a 1:1 mapping of vCPUs to physical cores. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA P4 GPU with 8 GB of dedicated VRAM.

The instance does not include any local storage, requiring external block storage volumes for operating system and application data. Network connectivity is limited to a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps, and the instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The lack of local storage and the modest network throughput represent key architectural tradeoffs for workloads requiring high-speed local disk I/O or massive network data transfers.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.gn5i-c2g1.large offers entry-level GPU acceleration within a compact resource footprint. The combination of a dedicated dual-core CPU, 8 GB of RAM, and an NVIDIA P4 GPU makes this instance suitable for lightweight GPU-accelerated workloads. Appropriate use cases include small-scale inference, video transcoding, basic machine learning model evaluation, and graphics rendering tasks that do not demand high-bandwidth network interfaces or large local storage arrays.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5i-c2g1.large is an entry-level, GPU-accelerated server instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated physical CPU cores with 1 thread per core, paired with 8.0 GB of system memory. Acceleration is delivered by a single NVIDIA P4 GPU with 8 GB of VRAM. The instance does not include local storage, relying entirely on external network-attached storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. This hardware profile represents a tradeoff, offering dedicated compute and GPU resources at a lower scale without local storage or high-speed networking. It is designed for lightweight GPU workloads such as small-scale inference, video transcoding, and basic graphics rendering.
